sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Which expression means: “Multiply 16 by 2, then subtract the product from 46.”
Which phrase describes 81 - (4 × 9) without evaluating it?
choices: Subtract 4 from 81, then multiply the difference by 9.
Multiply 4 by 9, then add the product to 81.
Add 81 and 4, then multiply the sum by 9.
Multiply 4 by 9, then subtract the product from 81.

items.prompt: Let E represent 815 + 3108. Without evaluating, how does (815 + 3108) + 106 compare with E?
choices: 106 times as large as E
105 greater than E
106 less than E
106 greater than E

items.prompt: A supply cart has 65 boxes with 27 markers in each box and 5 loose markers. Which expression represents the total number of markers?
A team packs 19 crates with 52 bottles in each crate, adds 91 loose bottles, and then uses 4 bottles. How many bottles remain?
In 9845539, how does the value of the 5 in the thousands place compare with the value of the 5 in the hundreds place?
choices: 100 times as much
1/10 as much
the same value
10 times as much

items.prompt: Round each number to the nearest thousand to estimate 560500 - 540500.
Round 350 to the nearest hundred and 25 to the nearest ten, then multiply to estimate the product.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: A student says 6594 - 5782 = 912. Round each number to the nearest hundred. Which choice correctly checks the claim?
choices: The claim is exact; the rounded estimate is 800.
The claim is not exact; the exact result is 812 and the rounded estimate is 900.
The claim is exact; the rounded estimate is 900.
The claim is not exact; the exact result is 812 and the rounded estimate is 800.

items.prompt: A student evaluates 2 × [15 + (24 - 12)] + 20: “They multiply 2 by 15 first, then finish the calculation, so the value is 62.” Which statement best identifies the error?
choices: The student multiplied before evaluating (24 - 12); the innermost difference is 12, giving 74.
The first error is in the final addition or subtraction; the value should be 75.
The work is correct; 62 is the value.
The student used the right first step but made an arithmetic slip; the value should be 76.

items.prompt: A student says, “In 3336779, the value of the 7 in the tens place is 100 times as much as the value of the 7 in the hundreds place.” Which statement best analyzes the error?
choices: The values are 70 and 700; 70 is 10 times as much as 700.
The values are 70 and 700; 70 is 100 times as much as 700, so the student's comparison is correct.
Both digits have value 7; repeated digits always have the same value.
The values are 70 and 700; 70 is 1/10 as much as 700, so the student's comparison is incorrect.
